purpose: Describe the write replacement protocol without promising unsupported filesystem atomicity.

protocol.incoming_snapshot: Persist the intended bytes and revision in app-owned recovery history before journaling prepared.
protocol.previous_snapshot: Persist the prior bytes and revision in app-owned recovery history before journaling prepared when the target exists.
protocol.temporary_file: Create a unique temporary file beside the target, write all bytes, and sync the file before replacement.
protocol.linux_and_macos: Use same-directory rename and rely on the mounted filesystem's documented semantics; network and sync filesystems are not certified by this fixture.
protocol.windows: Move the old target to an operation-scoped backup and then move the temporary file into place; this two-step fallback is not one atomic namespace replacement.
protocol.power_loss: The parent directory is not synced, so this protocol makes no universal power-loss durability claim.

acceptance: A prepared journal record is written only after required recovery images exist.
Replacement failures preserve the original target and incoming bytes where the filesystem permits.
No platform or filesystem is described as atomic unless its replacement behavior is established.
